query: For nanoparticles composed of five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios and initially crystallized as a solid solution, what governs whether structural and chemical stability is maintained across catalytic and thermoelectric operating ranges of 473–1923 K? Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis, specify a controlled comparison, predict observations relative to the initial baseline, define the conditions under which the prediction should hold, identify supporting evidence, and state a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Prolonged high-temperature annealing enhances atomic intermixing in HEA nanoparticles, reducing the tendency of less cohesive elements (e.g., Cu and Pd) to segregate to the surface. This uniform mixing preserves the solid-solution phase and maintains both structural and chemical stability under the catalytic and thermoelectric operating range of 473–1923 K.
generation.material_initial_state: HEA nanoparticles composed of five or more metals in equal or near‐equal atomic ratios, initially crystallized as a solid solution but potentially exhibiting slight atomic inhomogeneities.
generation.intervention: Apply prolonged high-temperature annealing (near the upper operating range, e.g., approaching 1923 K) for a duration sufficient to overcome kinetic diffusion barriers and achieve complete atomic mixing.
generation.conditions: Catalytic and thermoelectric operating environments maintained across 473–1923 K under inert or controlled atmosphere to minimize external oxidation or contamination.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced atomic interdiffusion leading to a uniformly mixed single-phase solid solution with minimized surface segregation (especially of Cu and Pd).
generation.mechanism: The high-temperature treatment increases atomic mobility so that atoms can overcome local free energy barriers. This uniform redistribution reduces the driving force for surface segregation of elements with lower cohesive energies, thereby maintaining a homogeneous phase even under challenging service conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: After annealing, HEA nanoparticles will exhibit a stable crystal lattice with little evidence of secondary phase formation or elemental segregation. In contrast, untreated particles are expected to develop significant surface compositional variations or segregated phases under the same conditions.
generation.baseline: As-synthesized HEA nanoparticles without prolonged annealing are expected to experience measurable segregation and phase instability during extended operation at high temperatures.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis holds if the annealing duration and temperature are high enough to enable diffusion without inducing melting or unwanted grain growth. Insufficient annealing time or temperature could fail to achieve full homogenization, while extreme conditions beyond the tested range might introduce additional degradation mechanisms.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal annealing duration and specific temperature profile needed for complete mixing are not precisely defined and may vary with the individual diffusion kinetics of the constituent metals.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of HEA nanoparticles: one treated with prolonged high-temperature annealing and one left untreated. Subject both groups to prolonged exposure under catalytic/thermoelectric conditions (473–1923 K) in a controlled atmosphere. After testing, perform structural and compositional analyses (using XRD, TEM-EDS, and XPS) to compare the degree of atomic homogeneity and surface segregation.
measurements: XRD (peak positions, peak widths for lattice integrity and phase purity)
TEM with EDS elemental mapping (to assess atomic distribution and detect segregation)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed (treated) nanoparticles exhibit the same or greater levels of phase segregation, formation of secondary phases, or surface compositional inhomogeneities compared to the untreated nanoparticles under the same high-temperature operating conditions, the hypothesis will be falsified.

Details of model development can be found in the Method section. Figure 3a presents a parity plot comparing DFT-calculated and ALIGNN-predicted per-atom energies. Both training and test data sets exhibit mean absolute errors (MAEs) below 5 meV/atom, indicating a balanced model without noticeable underfitting or overfitting. To determine the equilibrium surface configurations after high-temperature annealing, canonical Monte Carlo simulations were conducted using the trained deep learning potential, with an equilibrium achieved after approximately 16,000 steps. reading.lever: Apply prolonged high-temperature annealing to ensure complete atomic mixing and suppress detrimental surface segregation.
reading.why: This processing-route approach, demonstrated on multi-metal systems for homogeneous phase formation, directly addresses stability loss at elevated catalytic and thermoelectric operating temperatures.
